advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Compare source vs decoded HTML-comment occurrences by count (multiset), not substring membership, so a dropped duplicate also triggers the plain-encode fallback.
evidence: adf.py:439 `comments = _HTML_COMMENT_RE.findall(md)`
adf.py:442 `if any(comment not in decoded for comment in comments):` — substring test ignores multiplicity
ABSENCE: no count/multiset comparison of source vs decoded comment occurrences
advisory.finding: The HTML-comment content-preservation check uses `any(comment not in decoded for comment in comments)`, a substring membership test. If a comment appears MULTIPLE times in the source but the round-trip collapses it to fewer occurrences (or the same marker text appears twice and one copy is dropped), `comment not in decoded` is still False, so the partial content loss is not detected and the richer (lossy) encode is kept.
scenarios: A body with two identical HTML comment markers where the engine drops one
advisory.suggested_fix: Use `collections.Counter(_HTML_COMMENT_RE.findall(md)) != Counter(_HTML_COMMENT_RE.findall(decoded))` (or compare per-comment counts) to trigger the fallback.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that monkeypatches the marklas engine's to_adf/to_md to raise and asserts markdown_to_adf / adf_to_markdown return the plain text_to_adf / adf_to_text results (no exception propagates).
evidence: adf.py:444 `except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - any engine failure degrades, never propagates` then `return text_to_adf(md)`
adf.py:460 same pattern in adf_to_markdown returning `adf_to_text(doc)`
test_adf_markdown.py:113 test_cloud_functions_degrade_without_marklas covers only the `_marklas() is None` branch (monkeypatch sets _marklas to lambda: None), not an engine that raises
ABSENCE: no test in test_adf_markdown.py monkeypatches marklas.to_adf/to_md to raise and asserts the plain fallback is returned
advisory.finding: The engine-error degrade path in markdown_to_adf and adf_to_markdown (`except Exception: return text_to_adf(md)` / `return adf_to_text(doc)`) is untested: no test injects a raising marklas engine to prove conversion errors degrade to the plain result instead of propagating. The extra-absent path and the HTML-comment-drop path are covered, but the conversion-raises recovery contract the docstrings explicitly promise ('any engine failure degrades, never propagates') has no regression guard.
scenarios: marklas or mistune throws on a malformed body in production and the recovery must return the plain encode rather than crash the reconciler
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test using monkeypatch to set adf._marklas to return a stub whose to_adf/to_md raise, then assert adf.markdown_to_adf(md) == adf.text_to_adf(md) and adf.adf_to_markdown(doc) == adf.adf_to_text(doc).

evidence: scripts/build_cloud_adf_corpus.py substitutions: `("Success Criteria", "Acceptance Criteria"), ("success criteria", "acceptance criteria"), ("SUCCESS CRITERIA", "ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA")` — space-separated only
scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py:21: `PHRASE_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\b" + "success" + r"[ _-]criteri(?:a|on)\b", re.IGNORECASE)` matches `success_criteria`

scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py:68: `SOURCE_TEXT_SUFFIXES = frozenset({".py", ".md", ".json", ...})` — .json is scanned
scripts/criteria-vocabulary-allowlist.txt has no entry for tests/fixtures/cloud_adf_corpus/*, and check_criteria_vocabulary.py:49-52 EXCLUDED_FILES excludes only the generator, not the fixture
dropped.finding: The corpus scrub's `_VOCABULARY_SUBSTITUTIONS` only maps the space-separated variants of 'success criteria' (Success/success/SUCCESS Criteria), but the committed fixture contains the underscore form `migrate_success_criteria.py`, which the criteria-vocabulary guard matches case-insensitively via `success[ _-]criteri(a|on)`. The fixture (`tests/fixtures/cloud_adf_corpus/*.json`, a `.json` SOURCE_TEXT_SUFFIX scanned by the guard) is not in EXCLUDED_FILES nor the vocabulary allowlist, so the scrub does not actually render the committed fixture clean against the guard it claims to satisfy.
scenarios: `make lint` / the criteria-vocabulary guard scanning the committed corpus json
dropped.suggested_fix: Make the scrub match the guard: substitute using a regex equivalent to `success[ _-]criteri(a|on)` (case-insensitive) rather than three literal space-separated strings, and re-run the generator.
